claims.text: The alloy is initially a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Grain-boundary segregation is a primary mechanism governing toughness degradation in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Brittle grain-boundary precipitation is a primary mechanism governing toughness degradation in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Atom probe tomography can reveal the proposed grain-boundary segregation.
Atom probe tomography can reveal the proposed brittle grain-boundary precipitation.
Controlled introduction of grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation produces the proposed structural mediator.
Grain-boundary segregation causes brittle behavior to emerge in the high-entropy alloy.
Brittle grain-boundary precipitation causes brittle behavior to emerge in the high-entropy alloy.
The proposed behavior is relevant under both high- and low-temperature conditions.
The proposed behavior is relevant under various loading conditions.
Alloys with and without grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation should be compared using atom probe tomography and mechanical testing.
Similar toughness in alloys with and without the proposed grain-boundary features would falsify the hypothesis.
